title: Ancient Egypt & the Near East
description: Treasures of the Nile and Mesopotamia — gold, stone, and hieroglyph across five thousand years.
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Hippopotamus ("William")
items.description_narrative: This ancient Egyptian faience sculpture, affectionately known as "William," dates to approximately 1961–1878 B.C. Its vibrant blue-green glaze and intricate riverine decoration exemplify the artistry of the period.
items.tags: ancient egyptian, faience, hippopotamus, sculpture, animal art, artifact, middle kingdom
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: The Temple of Dendur
items.description_narrative: Carved from Aeolian sandstone, The Temple of Dendur is an ancient Egyptian temple that was completed by 10 B.C. This structure was moved in its entirety to New York and reconstructed within The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: ancient, egyptian, temple, architecture, religion, sandstone, historic
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Statuette of Amun
items.description_narrative: This exquisite statuette depicts Amun, one of the most important deities of ancient Egypt, rendered in solid gold. Its creation during Egypt's Third Intermediate Period reflects the enduring religious devotion and masterful craftsmanship of the era.
items.tags: ancient egypt, amun, deity, gold, sculpture, religious art, statuette, artifact
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Head of a ruler
items.description_narrative: This ancient Mesopotamian head, crafted from a copper alloy, depicts a powerful ruler from antiquity. Its detailed features and material signify a figure of importance from an early urban civilization.
items.tags: mesopotamian, ancient, sculpture, ruler, portrait, copper alloy, middle eastern
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Book of the Dead of Hunefer
items.description_narrative: This ancient Egyptian papyrus scroll, known as the Book of the Dead of Hunefer, served as a guide for the deceased through the underworld, ensuring a successful transition to the afterlife. It vividly illustrates various rituals and spells, most notably the iconic weighing of the heart ceremony before Osiris.
items.tags: ancient egypt, afterlife, funerary text, papyrus, hieroglyphics, weighing of the heart, ritualistic

items.title: Papyrus of Ani
items.description_narrative: The Papyrus of Ani is an ancient Egyptian funerary text, a magnificent example of the Book of the Dead, prepared for the scribe Ani. This richly illustrated scroll contains spells, prayers, and hymns intended to guide the deceased through the perils of the afterlife and ensure eternal existence.
items.tags: ancient egypt, funerary text, book of the dead, afterlife, hieroglyphs, illustrated manuscript, religious, spiritual

items.title: Seated Scribe
items.description_narrative: The Seated Scribe is an iconic ancient Egyptian sculpture renowned for its lifelike depiction of a scribe, poised with an unrolled papyrus. Its striking realism is heightened by the inlaid eyes, crafted from rock crystal and other materials, which convey a sense of immediacy and intelligence.
items.tags: ancient egypt, sculpture, scribe, old kingdom, realism, portrait, official
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art. See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

items.title: Faience Sphinx of Amenhotep III
items.description_narrative: This ancient Egyptian faience sphinx depicts Pharaoh Amenhotep III, symbolizing his divine power and royal authority. Crafted from a distinctive ceramic material, this sculpture reflects the sophisticated artistry of the New Kingdom.
items.tags: ancient egypt, sphinx, pharaoh, faience, sculpture, new kingdom, royalty
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art. See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

items.title: Wall Painting from the Tomb of Nebamun
items.description_narrative: This vibrant wall painting depicts scenes from the tomb of Nebamun, an ancient Egyptian scribe and grain accountant. It offers a detailed glimpse into idealized aspects of life and the afterlife, ranging from fowling in the marshes to banquets and garden scenes.
items.tags: ancient egypt, tomb painting, new kingdom, afterlife, daily life, fowling, banquet, stylized

items.title: Code of Hammurabi Stele
items.description_narrative: This ancient Babylonian stele features an elaborate cuneiform inscription of Hammurabi's legal code, presented beneath a high-relief carving depicting King Hammurabi receiving authority from the sun god Shamash. It stands as one of the earliest and most complete written legal codes, offering profound insights into ancient Mesopotamian society and justice.
items.tags: law, ancient, Mesopotamia, cuneiform, stele, history, legal code, Babylonian

items.title: Relief of a Winged Genius
items.description_narrative: This ancient relief depicts a winged genius, a powerful protective spirit often found guarding Assyrian palaces. Such figures embody divine authority and were carved to ward off evil and ensure the well-being of the ruler.
items.tags: assyrian, relief, sculpture, winged genius, protective spirit, ancient mesopotamia, mythological, monumental
items.credit_line: Neo-Assyrian Bas Relief of Winged Genius, from North Palace at Nimrud, c. 883-859 BC
